full_judgment:
3. The learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, by judgment and decree dated 31.8.76 decreed the suit holding that defendant No.1 was a defaulter and that defendant No.2 was not in ejmali possession of the suit shop. 

 4. Appellant took a revision against the said judgment and decree and also lost there. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 17 July, 1984 discharged the Rule in the said revision case whereupon appellant moved this Division and obtained leave to appeal. 

 5. The point raised was that when a title suit in respect of the entire ejmali property including the shop room was filed and later on decreed the S.C.C. suit was not maintainable as a co-sharer cannot eject another co-sharer from any part of the ejmali property. 

 6. At the hearing of the appeal, the learned Advocate for the appellant relied on the additional paper book filed by him and a photostat copy of the order sheet of Title Execution Case No.26 of 1985 of the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. It was pointed out that the preliminary decree dated 17.1.76 passed in the aforesaid partition suit was made final on 20.1.85 and that the decree holders obtained delivery of possession through Court and the execution case was disposed of upon full satisfaction by order dated 7.9.85. 

 7. In the concise statement filed by the appellant it has been stated that the preliminary decree in Title Suit No.168/73 was challenged in First Appeal No.42 of 1970 in the High Court but the appeal was dismissed on 13.7.77. It has been further stated that in terms of the final decree the appellant's possession in the suit premises has been left undisturbed and unaffected. These facts as stated by the learned advocate for the appellant an the basis of final decree, Advocate Commissioner's report etc. and assertions made in the concise statement have not been controverted before us on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent. In view of the subsequent development leading to the execution of the final decree in the partition suit, the learned' Advocate submits that the present appeal has become infructuous inasmuch as the decree passed in the S.C.C. suit has been rendered inexecutable. The submission of the learned Advocate goes uncontested.
